_note: The question set is original and SIG/CAIQ-style in structure only. It is not the SIG or the CAIQ. Weights, bands and rules are illustrative defaults.

questions.text: Do you maintain an approved information security policy that is reviewed at least annually?
Are you certified to ISO/IEC 27001 with a current certificate that covers the service we use?
Do you hold an independent SOC 2 Type 2 report that covers the service we use?
Do all staff complete security awareness training at least annually?
Is multi-factor authentication required for all remote access to systems that hold our data?
Is access to our data role-based, least-privilege and reviewed at least quarterly?
Is multi-factor authentication enforced for all privileged and administrator accounts?
Is access removed within one working day when staff leave or change role?
Is our data encrypted at rest?
Is our data encrypted in transit using current TLS versions?
Are encryption keys managed in a dedicated key management service with restricted access?
Is our data logically separated from other customers' data?
Do you have a documented incident response plan?
Is the incident response plan tested at least annually?
Will you notify us of a security incident affecting our data within 72 hours, or the contractual period if shorter?
Do you keep security logs for at least 12 months?
Do you have a documented business continuity and disaster recovery plan?
Is disaster recovery tested at least annually, with recorded results?
Are backups taken regularly and restore-tested at least annually?
Are recovery time and recovery point objectives defined for our service?
Do you scan your systems for vulnerabilities at least monthly?
Are critical vulnerabilities patched within 30 days?
Is an independent penetration test performed at least annually?
Is endpoint protection deployed and current on all devices that can access our data?
Do you follow a secure software development lifecycle that includes code review?
Do you scan code and dependencies for vulnerabilities before release?
Are production and test environments separated, with no live customer data in test?
Are changes to production approved and tracked?
Do you maintain a current list of the subprocessors and other third parties that touch our data?
Do you flow down security and confidentiality obligations to those third parties?
Do you assess the security of those third parties at least annually?
Will you tell us before you add or change a subprocessor that handles our data?

consistency.why: claims MFA for all remote access but no MFA for privileged accounts
claims the incident response plan is tested but says no plan exists
claims DR is tested but says no DR plan exists
claims managed encryption keys but says data is not encrypted at rest
claims to flow down obligations to third parties but keeps no list of them
claims to assess third parties but keeps no list of them
claims critical patching but does no vulnerability scanning
